boundaries.name: Historical Basemaps
boundaries.author: André Ourednik and contributors
boundaries.processing: Clipped to the map window (-30,12 to 62,72), slivers under 200 km² dropped, simplified to 8% with mapshaper, fields reduced to NAME, SUBJECTO and BORDERPRECISION.
boundaries.caveat: The maintainers describe the project as work in progress and ask that the maps be checked against other sources before academic use. Border precision is published per feature: 1 approximate, 2 moderately precise, 3 determined by treaty or law. Treat these outlines as an informed sketch of the political map, not as a surveyed boundary.
boundaries.gaps: Only 1800 and 1815 fall inside this atlas's span. There is no snapshot for 1805, 1812 or 1813, and none is interpolated.

archive.discovery: Wikimedia Commons API, searched per battle; only items the API reports as public domain or CC0 were kept.
archive.fields: Title, date, creator and licence are copied from the catalogue record. The holding institution is named from the credit line.
archive.nature: An item is marked a later depiction when the record's own evidence says so: a date well after the battle, or an engraver who was still a child at the time.
archive.linking: Entries link to the institution's catalogue where the record carries a resolvable URL, otherwise to the Wikimedia Commons record. No images are embedded: the page stays self-contained and no reuse terms are stretched.
archive.unverified: The Library of Congress refuses automated requests, so no LoC item is included. Gallica (BnF) also blocks scripts, but its two ark URLs here were opened in a browser and their titles checked against the catalogue record before being used.

tactical.sought: A dataset of troop positions, formations and movements with geographic calibration, for Austerlitz, Waterloo or Borodino.
tactical.found: Digitised battle plans as images only. A scanned plan is not a georeferenced dataset, and none of the sources surveyed publishes troop positions as coordinates.
tactical.consequence: Battle Lens shows the period plan as an archival document and links to its catalogue record. No troop positions, formations or battlefield geometry are drawn, because none could be sourced.
tactical.toResolve: A georeferenced battle dataset, or ground-control points allowing a scanned plan to be warped onto the map, each with licensing that permits redistribution.
